headline: Continued several wetland permit reviews; approved tree-cutting plans for sewer project and gas work; issued conditions for 71 N Billerica Road subdivision
summary: The Conservation Commission continued multiple Requests for Determination and a Notice of Intent to future meetings, including projects at 10 Old Ferry Road, 451 Black Brook Drive, Lowell Train Tack Right-Of-Way, 576 Lawrence Street, and 25.2 Market Street. It approved Standard Orders of Conditions and negative (-3) determinations for several other projects, and ratified an Enforcement Order for a wetlands violation at 52 Ostrander Ave.
decisions: Continued the Request for Determination of Applicability for Vicki O'Neil at 10 Old Ferry Road to the 8/26 meeting.
Referred the question of whether peer review is required to the Law Department.
Continued the Winn Co. Request for Determination of Applicability at 451 Black Brook Drive to the September 23 meeting.
Issued a Standard Order of Conditions with two conditions for the FTO Realty Trust Notice of Intent at 71 N Billerica Road, passed 3-1.
Continued the CSX Transportation Request for Determination of Applicability for the Lowell Train Tack Right-Of-Way to the 8/26 meeting.
Issued a -3 determination for Centennial Island Housing, L.P. at 576 Lawrence Street.
Issued a -3 determination for Alex Bail/Albanese D&S Inc. at 61 First Street Boulevard.
Closed the public hearing for the Wexford Science & Technology Notice of Intent at 256.2 Market Street.
Continued the Wexford Science & Technology matter at 256.2 Market Street to the 8/26 meeting.
Issued a -3 determination for Boston Gas Company at 1-20 Saunders Street ROW.
Ratified the Enforcement Order against the property at 52 Ostrander Ave.

plain_text:
CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
LOWELL, MASSACHUSETTS 
July 22, 2026 
Note: These minutes are not completed verbatim. For further detail, video recordings are available at 
the Pollard Library, second floor reference desk or online at www.LTC.org. 
This meeting was held both in person and virtually using Zoom. 
Members Present:  Chairman Brad Buitenhuys, Vice -Chair Perry Downs , Commissioner Marie Burns , 
Commissioner Kristin Ross-Sitcawich, Commissioner Roberto Ciccarelli 
Members Absent:  
Others Present: Peter Cutrumbes, Assistant Planner 
CALL TO ORDER 
ORDER OF BUSINESS 
CONTINUED BUSINESS 
Vicki O’Neil  
31 Anderson Way  
Tyngsborough, MA 01879  
Project Location: 10 Old Ferry Road, 01854  
A Request for Determination of Applicability has been filed by Vicki O'Neil to construct a single-family 
home at 10 Old Ferry Road. The applicant is seeking to determine whether the proposed work 
is located within the 100-foot buffer zone of a wetland resource area.  
On Behalf: 
Matt Hamor, the applicant’s engineer and representative. 
 
In Favor: 
None 
 
In Opposition: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
B. Buitenhuys noted the applicant requested a continuance but also requested that the Commission 
speak with the City’s legal team about whether peer review is actually required. He is supportive of that. 
Motion: 
P. Downs motioned to continue the matter to the 8/26 meeting. R. Ciccarelli seconded. The vote was 
unanimous (5-0).
P. Downs motioned to send the issue to the Law Department. R Ciccarelli seconded. The vote was 
unanimous (5-0). 
 
Request for Determination of Applicability 
Winn Co. 
50 Braintree Hill Office Park, Suite 304 
Braintree, MA 02184 
Project Location: 451 Black Brook Drive, 01851 
A Request for Determination of Applicability has been filed by Winn Co. Seeking approval to clean out 
the existing culvert at 451 Black Brook Drive. The activity will occur within the 100-foot wetland buffer 
zone. 
 
On Behalf: 
None 
 
In Favor: 
None 
 
In Opposition: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
None 
 
Motion: 
P. Downs motioned to continue the matter to the September 23 meeting. R. Ciccarelli seconded. The 
vote was unanimous (5-0). 
 
Notice of Intent 
FTO Realty Trust 
109 Blanchard Road 
Lawrence, MA 01843 
DEP #: 206-0853 
Project Location: 71 N Billerica Road, 01852 
A Notice of Intent has been filed by FTO Realty Trust to subdivide the property into 11 single-family 
homes at 71 North Billerica Road. Portions of the project are within the 100-foot buffer zone of a 
Bordering Vegetated Wetland (BVW) and/or the 100-year floodplain. 
 
*Chairman Buitenhuys recused himself from this matter* 
 
On Behalf: 
Attorney John Cox, the applicant’s lawyer. The project came before the Commission on June 10 and 
there was a lengthy discussion. On May 4 it received Planning Board approval. At the end of the 
discussion on June 10, a tree survey was asked for. This survey has been completed. The City’s Engineer 
has signed off on the porous pavement. There are no adverse comments from DEP, and no violation of 
the 50-foot no-build zone.
Matt Hamor, the applicant’s engineer, discussed the tree survey. He located all trees with a DBH of 24’ 
or greater. There are 6 trees within the 50-100 foot buffer. 8 trees were identified within the 100-Year 
Flood Plain. The project team showed the tree mitigation on the plans. The original plans had 9 trees 
along the roadway. The Planning Board recommended three trees on each lot. This would be a total of 
42 trees. 
 
In Favor: 
None 
 
In Opposition: 
Stacey Decker 110 Hollis Street. She stated that preserving and planting trees is critical in combatting 
climate change. The trees on this property are very important. Their homes are important to them, and 
they cannot predict the future outcomes on their homes after the construction of this subdivision. They 
still have concerns regarding things such as basement flooding. She has one final ask: that the applicant 
retains the tree line between the existing homes and the proposed project. 
 
Discussion: 
R. Ciccarelli asked about the preservation of the tree line. Will the proposed new trees be in the same 
area as the existing trees? M. Hamor said the trees he discussed are in the construction zone. The new 
trees will not be in the exact same spots. He noted there are two large trees on the property line and 
they are willing to leave those two. J. Cox confirmed he talked to the developer and he agrees. 
 
Motion: 
R. Ciccarelli motioned to issue a City of Lowell Standard Order of Conditions along with the following 
conditions: 
1. The two existing trees on the property line to be preserved 
2. The applicant shall mark out the wetland boundary on the rear of the property. 
 
M. Burns seconded. The vote passed, 3-1. K. Ross-Sitcawich voted in dissent and B. Buitenhuys recused 
himself from the vote. 
 
Request for Determination of Applicability 
CSX Transportation 
500 Water Street 
Jacksonville, FL 32202 
Project Location: Lowell Train Tack Right-Of-Way 
A Request for Determination of Applicability has been filed by CSX Transportation, Inc, regarding their 
plans for weed control via herbicide. The applicant is seeking to determine where the proposed work is 
located within the 100-foot buffer zone of a wetland resource area. 
 
On Behalf: 
None 
 
In Favor: 
None
In Opposition: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
The applicant requested a continuance. 
 
Motion: 
M. Burns motioned to continue the matter to the 8/26 meeting. K. Ross-Sitcawich seconded. The vote 
was unanimous (5-0). 
 
NEW BUSINESS: 
 
Request for Determination of Applicability 
Centennial Island Housing, L.P. 
30 Hudson Yards 
New York, NY 10001 
Project Location: 576 Lawrence Street, 01852 
A Request for Determination of Applicability has been filed by Centennial Island Housing, L.P. to engage 
in maintenance work on the property. The work includes activities such as repaving, replacing sidewalks 
and curbs, and updating fencing. A portion of the work is within 25 feet of the Concord River and the 
100-foot buffer zone of River Meadow Brook. 
 
On Behalf: 
Brandon Lambert, the applicant’s Engineer. The area of work is located on the site of an old mill 
complex. There are three buildings on site and multiple parking areas, sidewalks, and landscaped areas. 
The property is bounded by Lawrence Street and the Concord River. River Meadow Brook bisects the 
property. The plan shows buffer zones of 25 feet, 50 feet, and 100 feet from the river and the brook. 
The majority of the project is maintenance. They are not expanding the development footprint. Most of 
the work is repaving the parking lot. The repaving will be a 2-inch milling off the top of the existing 
pavement, and then repaving that. There are two small areas that need to be repaved to full depth. 
They are also replacing a dumpster pad, sidewalks, fencing, and granite curbing. Also replacing the slope 
granite curb with concrete curb. Protecting waterways by using erosion control on the downhill portions 
of the site and on the waterways themselves. Pavement milling leftovers go right into the back of the 
truck and leaves the site the same day. Equipment isn’t stored onsite. There will only be 1-2 days of 
exposed ground during the replacement of pavement or sidewalks. 
 
In Favor: 
None 
 
 
In Opposition: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
B. Buitenhuys noted that there is a parking lot at the rear of the property that is overgrown. It is not on 
this plan, but he would like to see the applicant clean that up. He said he has no issues with the project. 
 
Motion:
P. Downs motioned to issue a –3 determination. M. Burns seconded. The vote was unanimous (5-0). 
 
Request for Determination of Applicability 
Alex Bail 
66 Silva Lane 
Dracut, MA 01826 
Project Location: 61 First Street Boulevard, 01850 
 A Request for Determination of Applicability has been filed by Albanese D&S Inc. to assess whether the 
area of work at 61 First Street Boulevard is in the jurisdiction of the Wetlands Protection Act (WPA), and 
whether the planned work is subject to the WPA. The work will include cutting down 43 trees in order 
to expand the staging area for the Centralville Sewer Separation project. 
 
 
On Behalf: 
Gorden Bergeron from the Lowell Regional Wastewater Utility and Peter Luciani from Albanese. G. 
Bergeron said that the sewer separation project is one of the largest DPW projects in the City’s history. 
Currently they are using the address as the staging area, Multiple crews are working simultaneously on 
this project. They have run out of space for staging so they are requesting to remove more trees. A lot of 
the trees that are being removed are invasive, like Norway Maples. Intention of removing the trees here 
is to keep all the work consolidated to one site, as opposed to having multiple staging areas.  
 
In Favor: 
None 
 
In Opposition: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
B. Buitenhuys asked how many trees were invasive. G. Bergeron said 6. 2 of the trees are also 
considered in poor condition as assessed by a professional arborist. He noted that tree #143 was 
requested by the Planning Board to be kept. B. Buitenhuys asked what the replanting plan is. G. 
Bergeron said the trees will be restored completely after work, and the invasives will be replaced with 
natives. In the meantime, 12 trees will be planted at other municipal properties. B. Buitenhuys said 
LRWWU and DPW are doing a great job on the sewer separation project. He knows a full restoration is 
being planned, and in combination with the planting of trees in the meantime, this is something he is 
inclined to support. 
 
Motion: 
M. Burns motioned to issue a –3 determination. K. Ross-Sitcawich seconded. The vote was unanimous 
(5-0). 
 
Notice of Intent 
Wexford Science & Technology, LLC 
4 N Martin Luther King Jr Blvd, Suite 500 
Baltimore, MD 21201 
Project Location: 256.2 Market Street, 01852
A Notice of Intent has been filed by Wexford Science & Technology LLC to construct a commercial 
building at 25.2 Market Street. The proposed work will take place within the 100-foot buffer zone to the 
bank of a canal. 
 
On Behalf: 
Conor Nagle, the Civil Engineer from the project for VHB and Chase Bernier, the Environmental Scientist 
for the project. 
 
This project is Parcel 15. The lot itself is 1.2 acres. The project would use the adjacent Parcel 16 as a lay 
down area. It is an existing, closed-off parking lot. Wexford Development is seeking to bring a Research 
and Development office to Parcel 15. The building  footprint will be approximately 35,000 square feet in 
area and 3 stories high. They are improving the drainage in the area as it currently almost all impervious. 
Right now the parking lot drains into the Merrimack Canal. They will be running the outfall through 
stormwater treatment before it enters the canal. Erosion control will be setup to prevent anything 
getting anything into the canal. They have been approved by the Historic Board and the ZBA. 
 
In Favor: 
None 
 
In Opposition: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
B. Buitenhuys asked if the lot was the most recent home of the giant pile of dirt that was recently 
removed. They usually don’t get too deep into canal work here. He is sure this has been under close 
scrutiny. The only major concern would be dumping snow or sand into the canal. Staff comments 
recommended they receive a stormwater permit, but they probably will have to anyway. C. Nagle said 
the project team is meeting with the DPW about this permit on Friday. B. Buitenhuys said anything is a 
better use of this land than what it currently is. He is comfortable with the projects. He noted there is no 
MassDEP filing number so they cannot technically approve it tonight. 
 
Motion: 
M. Burns motioned to close the public hearing. R. Ciccarelli seconded. The motion was unanimous (5-0). 
 
P. Downs motioned to continue to the 8/26 meeting. R. Ciccarelli seconded. The motion was unanimous 
(5-0). 
 
Request for Determination of Applicability  
Boston Gas Company  
170 Data Drive  
Waltham, MA 02451  
Project Location: 1-20 Saunders Street ROW, 01851   
A Request for Determination of Applicability has been filed by the Boston Gas Company seeking a 
determination to confirm there are no jurisdictional areas subject to the Massachusetts Wetlands 
Protection or Lowell Wetlands Bylaw at 1-20 Saunders Street ROW. 
 
On Behalf:
Kelan Koncewicz from VHB the applicant’s representative. The work will take place in the ROW of 
Saunders Street. They will install approximately 190 feet of 2” plastic pipe along Saunders 
Street between Middlesex and Payne Streets; and cut, cap and abandon approximately 250 feet of 4” 
gas main on Saunders Street between Middlesex Street to 20 Payne Street. It is within 100-feet of a 
canal. B. Buitenhuys asked if all the work is underneath the paved roadway. K. Koncewicz confirmed. 
 
In Favor: 
None 
 
In Opposition: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
None 
 
Motion: 
P. Downs motioned to issue a –3 determination. M. Burns seconded. The vote was unanimous (5-0). 
  
Enforcement Order  
FVD and MOD Family and Realty Irrevocable Trust  
52 Ostrander Ave  
Lowell, MA 01851  
Violation Location: 52 Ostrander Ave, 01851  
An Enforcement Order has been issued against 52 Ostrander Ave. The violator has cut trees within the 
100-Year FEMA Flood Zone as well as deposited the cuttings and other debris within 100 feet of Black 
Brook. 
 
On Behalf: 
The property owner. They cut 30 arborvitae shrubs between 2 houses. He did not know there are 
wetlands on this property. The trees were falling down. He did not dump on the City property across the 
street—he has the receipt for the stumps being taken away. It is a common dumping site for the 
neighborhood.  They are replacing the arborvitaes in kind. 
 
In Favor: 
None 
 
In Opposition: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
B. Buitenhuys said that the area across the street did not appear to be materials that were from 
removing the shrubs. He asked the property owner to send us photos when its done. 
 
Motion: 
PD ratify MB seconded 
P. Downs motioned to ratify the Enforcement Order. M. Burns seconded. The motion was unanimous (5-
0).
OTHER BUSINESS  
 
6/24/2026 meeting minutes  
M. Burns motioned to accept the minutes. K. Ross-Sitcawich seconded. The vote was unanimous (5-0). 
 
ADJOURNMENT 
P. Downs motioned to adjourn. The meeting was adjourned at 7:54 PM.
